description: We are a team of three passionate individuals with experience in multiple programming languages, artificial intelligence, software development, and space science. Our mission is to develop an innovative software solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge by combining advanced technologies, creativity, and scientific thinking. We aim to tackle real-world challenges related to space exploration through teamwork, research, and problem-solving. We are excited to turn our ideas into reality!
summary:
What happens to a space explorer after its mission ends?

Space Story is a story-driven, browser-based hidden-object game that reconnects young learners with the machines humanity left beyond Earth. Players travel through the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space, searching illustrated pixel-art scenes for historic spacecraft and instruments.

Each discovery unlocks a collectible card. Flip it to explore a real NASA photograph, the mission’s purpose, its scientific contributions, and the story behind the hardware, with links to official NASA sources.

Designed primarily for ages 10–16 and casual space enthusiasts, Space Story transforms technical mission histories into an approachable journey of discovery. A proximity radar supports players who need help, while a personal collection lets them revisit recovered stories.

Our message is simple: a mission can end without its story being over.
details:
THE IDEA

Space exploration is often told through launches, first discoveries, and active missions. But what happens to the machines that remain when those missions end?

Space Story invites players to recover their stories. We created an educational hidden-object adventure for school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts, responding to the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge.

THE EXPERIENCE

The journey begins with a cinematic introduction and an explorer callsign. Players then choose one of three destinations: the Moon, Mars, or Deep Space.

Each sector contains missions set in detailed pixel-art search scenes. A short briefing introduces the target and gives players a reason to look for it. Some scenes contain two explorers to recover, encouraging players to notice differences between related machines.

Players can activate a radar hint once per scene. For five seconds, its signal becomes faster as the pointer approaches an undiscovered target.

Finding an artifact unlocks its collectible card. The front presents its pixel-art identity; the reverse connects that illustration to a real NASA photograph and an educational mission profile. Cards explain what the machine was, why it was sent, where it belongs, what it contributed to science, and what happened to it.

Recovered cards remain accessible through the field archive and collection menu during the session. Completed sectors are marked on the selection screen. Completing all sectors unlocks an expedition certificate and a return-to-Earth ending.

STORYTELLING AND SCIENCE

Our central narrative is that these machines are more than abandoned objects: they are evidence of human curiosity and scientific progress.

The collection includes Apollo equipment, Surveyor, Mars rovers and landers, Ingenuity, and deep-space explorers such as Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer, and Kepler.

NASA mission histories provide the factual foundation. We translate those resources into short, readable explanations and retain source links so players can continue learning.

The search environments are imaginative illustrations, not geographic maps or reconstructions of actual landing sites. The information cards distinguish these artistic scenes from the missions’ real locations and histories.

DESIGN AND TECHNOLOGY

Space Story is built with React, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Vite. It runs in a web browser without installation. Session storage records collected cards and mission progress during play.

A consistent retro interface connects the introduction, exploration scenes, collectible cards, and ending. Separate music and sound-effect controls let players adjust the audio experience.

IMPACT

Space Story aims to make learners curious enough to ask what each machine discovered and why it still matters. It combines observation, exploration, and reading in a format that encourages players to revisit scientific stories.

The current project is a playable educational prototype. Its learning outcomes have not yet been formally evaluated with students.
